definitions.explanation: A large-scale earthquake causing significant damage. Japan uses this term frequently due to its location on major fault lines and history of devastating earthquakes.

examples.japanese: {大地震|おおじしん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{起|お}きた→起きる：00521_okiru⟧。
{大地震|おおじしん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{備|そな}えて→備える：02125_sonaeru⟧⟦{防災|ぼうさい}グッズ→防災グッズ：23509_bousaiguzzu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{準備|じゅんび}した→準備する：22427_junbisuru⟧。
examples.english: I prepared disaster supplies in case of a major earthquake.

examples.japanese: ⟦{専門家|せんもんか}→専門家：03088_senmonka⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{今後|こんご}→今後：02808_kongo⟧{三十年|さんじゅうねん}⟦{以内|いない}→以内：01317_inai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{大地震|おおじしん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{発生|はっせい}する→発生する：25529_hasseisuru⟧⟦{確率|かくりつ}→確率：00159_kakuritsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{警告|けいこく}→警告：02696_keikoku⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Experts warn that there is a high probability of a major earthquake occurring within the next thirty years.

notes:
PRONUNCIATION:
Both おおじしん and だいじしん are used. おおじしん is the traditional reading and is used by NHK and most media. だいじしん is also widely accepted.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japan experiences frequent earthquakes, and {大地震|おおじしん} is a word that appears regularly in news and disaster preparedness materials. Major historical earthquakes include the ⟦{関東|かんとう}→関東：00186_kantou⟧{大震災|だいしんさい} (1923 Great Kanto Earthquake) and the {東日本|ひがしにほん}{大震災|だいしんさい} (2011 Great East Japan Earthquake).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大地震|おおじしん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{起|お}きる→起きる：00521_okiru⟧: a major earthquake occurs
- {大地震|おおじしん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{備|そな}える→備える：02125_sonaeru⟧: to prepare for a major earthquake
- {大地震|おおじしん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{被害|ひがい}→被害：02572_higai⟧: damage from a major earthquake
- {大地震|おおじしん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{発生|はっせい}する→発生する：25529_hasseisuru⟧: a major earthquake strikes
